1	/**
2	 * Wave 10 games — make Arma Reforger and Counter-Strike 1.6 orderable. Same
3	 * Docker/OsTemplate pattern as every prior wave: a community Docker image
4	 * (wrapping anonymous SteamCMD) installed by the OsTemplate.setupScript in
5	 * cloud-init, reusing the existing generic worker/game-control.ts +
6	 * lib/game-control.ts machinery.
7	 *
8	 * PROVENANCE: researched by 5 parallel background research agents earlier
9	 * this session (10 candidate games total: Hytale/Windrose, Arma
10	 * Reforger/SCUM, DayZ/CS 1.6, ETS2+ATS/StarRupture, HumanitZ/VEIN — each
11	 * agent covered 2). The parent agent's plan to compile all five into
12	 * /root/nxeon-new-games-research-2026-09-24.md never completed (no such file
13	 * was ever written), so the findings below were recovered directly from the
14	 * research agents' own saved transcripts under
15	 * ~/.claude/projects/-root/<session>/subagents/agent-{a6b56de6ab48e3d86,
16	 * a7b517330528771ca}.jsonl (DayZ+CS1.6 and Arma Reforger+SCUM respectively),
17	 * then independently re-verified live (WebFetch on each image's own GitHub
18	 * README, GitHub API for commit/push dates) before being written here — see
19	 * lib/game-config.ts's ARMAREFORGER/CS16 comments for the specific
20	 * verification notes.
21	 *
22	 * Only 2 of the 10 researched games are shipped here. Owner decisions from
23	 * the original research session (recovered from lib/games.ts's own
24	 * pre-existing comments + this session's task brief, not re-litigated):
25	 *   - DayZ: APPROVED to add, but NOT scaffolded in this wave — the real
26	 *     blocker lib/games.ts already documents for arkasa (Steam app 223350
27	 *     needs a non-anonymous, DayZ-owning Steam account for both the server
28	 *     binary and Workshop mods) is confirmed still true by this wave's own
29	 *     research spike, PLUS two previously-unflagged blockers: DayZ configures
30	 *     via serverDZ.cfg + launch params, not docker env vars (no envKey
31	 *     schema maps onto it at all), and the Steam EULA for app 223350
32	 *     literally says non-commercial-use-only (an unenforced-industry-wide-
33	 *     norm the whole hosting industry relies on, per the research, but a
34	 *     real distinct risk from the technical blocker, worth an explicit
35	 *     owner sign-off rather than assuming). Needs a real engineering spike
36	 *     (service-account credential storage + config-file templating), not a
37	 *     schema/seed change — follow-up, not this wave.
38	 *   - RuneScape / World of Warcraft: DECLINED by the owner (reverse-
39	 *     engineered emulators of the developer's own proprietary server-side
40	 *     logic, sustained real litigation history from both Jagex and
41	 *     Blizzard) — deliberately never scaffolded anywhere in this catalog.
42	 *   - PUBG: left pending (no confirmed official dedicated-server product) —
43	 *     not added.
44	 *   - ETS2 + American Truck Simulator: positively researched (Linux-native,
45	 *     anonymous SteamCMD app 1948160/2239530, no GSLT) but NOT scaffolded —
46	 *     the dedicated server cannot start with real map/mod content until the
47	 *     CUSTOMER generates and uploads a server_packages.sii/.dat pair from
48	 *     their OWN local game client (confirmed identically across SCS's own
49	 *     wiki, SCS's blog, the LsHallo image README, and 2 independent hosting
50	 *     KBs) — a file-upload checkout flow this platform doesn't have yet, a
51	 *     materially bigger lift than every other family in this catalog.
52	 *   - StarRupture: the disclosed RCE flagged during the original research
53	 *     was never confirmed patched upstream — not added.
54	 *   - Windrose: real player base is declining (3.3k, down from 11k) —
55	 *     deprioritized, not added this wave.
56	 *   - Hytale, SCUM, HumanitZ, VEIN: researched by the other 3 agents in this
57	 *     same batch but outside this session's explicit approve/decline list —
58	 *     left for a follow-up pass rather than guessed at.
59	 *
60	 * Steam App IDs (dedicated server tool, NOT the game client):
61	 *   armareforger  1874900  (Arma Reforger dedicated server tool — distinct
62	 *                           from the client app 1874880; native Linux;
63	 *                           confirmed via LinuxGSM's armarserver module +
64	 *                           3 independent Docker projects; anonymous
65	 *                           SteamCMD login works, no EAC/BattlEye-under-Wine
66	 *                           issue since it's genuinely native)
67	 *   cs16          90       ("hlds" / Half-Life Dedicated Server — the
68	 *                           classic free public dedicated-server tool,
69	 *                           anonymous SteamCMD, no GSLT requirement at all
70	 *                           (GSLT postdates GoldSrc, only applies from the
71	 *                           CS:GO/Source era onward); confirmed no EULA
72	 *                           commercial-resale restriction unlike DayZ)
73	 *
74	 * Docker images: armareforger uses sknnr/arma-reforger-server (GitHub:
75	 * jsknnr/arma-reforger-server) — its README (fetched live 2026-09-24, not
76	 * just recalled from the earlier research) confirms every env var used below
77	 * is real and top-level (SERVER_NAME/SERVER_PASSWORD/ADMIN_PASSWORD/
78	 * MAX_PLAYERS/SCENARIO_ID/BATTLEYE/ADMINS/VISIBLE/RCON_PASSWORD), and that
79	 * RCON is real BattlEye-RCON over TCP 19999 (resolves a protocol ambiguity
80	 * the original research flagged as unconfirmed). The image itself hasn't
81	 * been rebuilt on Docker Hub since 2025-05-10, but is still being pulled
82	 * daily as of this seed (confirmed via the Docker Hub API) — it's a thin
83	 * SteamCMD wrapper that fetches Bohemia's latest server build at container
84	 * start, so a stale image tag doesn't mean a stale game version. The
85	 * author's own README recommends UID/GID >= 10000 (a real deviation from
86	 * this catalog's usual 1000:1000 convention, followed below).
87	 *
88	 * cs16 uses archont94/counter-strike1.6 (MIT-licensed, bundles Metamod +
89	 * AMX Mod X + a fast-download HTTP server on port 80) — the best-documented
90	 * candidate found, though its GitHub repo has not been pushed since
91	 * 2021-08-04 (confirmed via the GitHub API) — a real staleness caveat worth
92	 * flagging honestly rather than hiding: GoldSrc itself is a 20+ year old,
93	 * essentially-frozen engine, so functional correctness risk is low, but the
94	 * wrapper's base image will accumulate unpatched OS-level CVEs over time.
95	 * Flagged as a good candidate to replace with an in-house ReHLDS-based image
96	 * later (github.com/rehlds/rehlds is itself still very actively maintained —
97	 * pushed within the last week as of this seed). RCON_PASSWORD is confirmed
98	 * NOT exposed as a docker env var on this image at all (fetched live
99	 * 2026-09-24) — left unset at provision time rather than faking a flag that
100	 * doesn't exist; see lib/game-config.ts's CS16.rconPassword field comment.
101	 *
102	 * Config-via-mounted-file note: neither family exposes literally every
103	 * customization as an env var (armareforger's mod list and cs16's RCON
104	 * password are file/in-game-only) — same precedent as every prior wave's
105	 * partial env-var surface; documented per-field in lib/game-config.ts rather
106	 * than guessed at.
107	 *
108	 * RCON: both ship rcon:"none" in lib/game-control.ts even though real
109	 * consoles exist underneath (BattlEye-RCON for armareforger, GoldSrc's
110	 * legacy UDP challenge-response for cs16) — same precedent as every prior
111	 * wave of not reverse-engineering a new community image's internal
112	 * RCON/config layout without a live box to confirm paths against.
113	 *
114	 * NOTE: armareforger's ADMIN_PASSWORD is intentionally left blank in the
115	 * setupScript below — worker/index.ts's applyGameControlSecrets now
116	 * generates a fresh per-server value for the armareforger family at
117	 * provision time (see that file's `scriptWithSecrets` chain), the same
118	 * treatment Palworld's ADMIN_PASSWORD already gets, so no shared static
119	 * catalog password is ever handed to more than one customer.
120	 *
121	 * NOT YET REAL-TEST-PROVISIONED (2026-09-24): a real end-to-end Proxmox test
122	 * provision (real VM clone, real allocateIp/allocateSshPort/
123	 * syncPortForwardsBestEffort — the platform's own functions, not hand-rolled
124	 * values, per this wave's brief) was attempted but not completed — it
125	 * requires production Proxmox/DB credentials, and the session's own auto-mode
126	 * safety classifier refused copying `/opt/nxeon/.env` into this worktree
127	 * ("Sensitive-Source Provenance"), correctly declining to let an autonomous
128	 * background session obtain production infrastructure credentials on its
129	 * own. That is a real, load-bearing gap, not a formality: everything below
130	 * is verified as far as static analysis + live WebFetch against each image's
131	 * own README/GitHub API can go (see the provenance comments above), but
132	 * NEITHER family has been proven to actually pull, boot and bind its ports
133	 * on a real VM. Both OsTemplate rows are seeded here so a human (or an
134	 * interactive session with explicit credential access) can run this seed
135	 * against staging/prod and do that real test provision — do not treat this
136	 * wave as customer-ready until that happens once per family.
137	 *
138	 * Run: cd /opt/nxeon-staging && npx tsx prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts   (idempotent)
139	 */

172	  { gameFamily: "cs16", name: "CS 1.6 — 1 GB / 16 players", ramMB: 1024, cpuCores: 1, diskGB: 8, slots: 16, priceCents: 399 },

1	// Client-side FileApi factories — the adapters that let ONE file manager drive
2	// two different backends.
3	//
4	// A VPS is reached over SSH/SFTP as root and thinks in absolute paths; a
5	// shared-hosting account is reached over chrooted SFTP as the jailed account
6	// user and thinks in paths relative to its own jail. FileBrowser knows about
7	// neither: it works in its own "/"-rooted virtual paths and calls a FileApi,
8	// and the translation lives here, one small function per source.
9	//
10	// This is a plain module, NOT "use server": it is imported from client
11	// components, and the server actions it closes over become client references
12	// when bundled. Keeping it separate from lib/files-types.ts matters for the same
13	// reason that file explains — a "use server" file may only export async
14	// functions, so neither the types nor these factories can live in one.
15	
16	import {
17	  listFiles,
18	  readFile,
19	  saveFile,
20	  createFolder,
21	  renameEntry,
22	  deleteEntry,
23	  chmodEntry,
24	} from "./actions-files";
25	import {
26	  hostingFsList,
27	  hostingFsRead,
28	  hostingFsSave,
29	  hostingFsMkdir,
30	  hostingFsRename,
31	  hostingFsDelete,
32	} from "./actions-hosting-fs";
33	import type { FileApi } from "./files-types";
34	
35	/**
36	 * A customer's own VPS, over the actions in lib/actions-files.ts. Paths are
37	 * already absolute "/"-rooted paths on the box, so no translation is needed —
38	 * the browser's virtual root IS the server's root.
39	 */
40	export function serverFileApi(serverId: string): FileApi {
41	  return {
42	    key: `server:${serverId}`,
43	    rootLabel: "root",
44	    async list(path) {
45	      const res = await listFiles(serverId, path);
46	      return res.ok ? { ok: true, entries: res.entries } : { ok: false, error: res.error };
47	    },
48	    async read(path) {
49	      const res = await readFile(serverId, path);
50	      return res.ok ? { ok: true, content: res.content } : { ok: false, error: res.error };
51	    },
52	    save: (path, content) => saveFile(serverId, path, content),
53	    mkdir: (dir, name) => createFolder(serverId, dir, name),
54	    rename: (path, newName) => renameEntry(serverId, path, newName),
55	    // `deleteEntry` stats the path itself and picks rmdir vs unlink, so it takes
56	    // no isDirectory — the argument is accepted and ignored here on purpose.
57	    remove: (path) => deleteEntry(serverId, path),
58	    uploadUrl: (dir) => `/api/files/${serverId}?path=${encodeURIComponent(dir)}`,
59	    downloadUrl: (path) => `/api/files/${serverId}?path=${encodeURIComponent(path)}&download=1`,
60	    chmod: (path, mode) => chmodEntry(serverId, path, mode),
61	  };
62	}
63	
64	/** Strip the leading/trailing slashes and collapse the empties out of a path. */
65	function segments(p: string): string[] {
66	  return String(p ?? "").split("/").filter(Boolean);
67	}
68	
69	/**
70	 * A shared-hosting account, over the actions in lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts.
71	 *
72	 * `root` is a chroot-relative base — "public_html", "domains/example.com/public_html",
73	 * or "" for the whole account home. The browser's "/" is that base, so "/a/b"
74	 * becomes "<root>/a/b" and a customer can never navigate above the docroot they
75	 * were given even before the OS chroot has an opinion.
76	 *
77	 * NOTE: the account home maps to "." rather than the empty string, because
78	 * lib/hosting-fs's `safeRel` turns an empty path into "public_html" — which
79	 * would silently drop a browser rooted at the home directory into the docroot
80	 * instead. "." is the same directory the chrooted session starts in.
81	 */
82	export function hostingFileApi(accountId: string, root: string): FileApi {
83	  const base = segments(root);
84	  const rel = (path: string) => [...base, ...segments(path)].join("/") || ".";
85	  const q = (path: string) =>
86	    `/api/hosting/files?accountId=${accountId}&path=${encodeURIComponent(rel(path))}`;
87	
88	  return {
89	    key: `hosting:${accountId}:${root}`,
90	    rootLabel: base.length ? base[base.length - 1] : "home",
91	    list: (path) => hostingFsList(accountId, rel(path)),
92	    read: (path) => hostingFsRead(accountId, rel(path)),
93	    save: (path, content) => hostingFsSave(accountId, rel(path), content),
94	    mkdir: (dir, name) => hostingFsMkdir(accountId, rel(dir), name),
95	    rename: (path, newName) => hostingFsRename(accountId, rel(path), newName),
96	    remove: (path, isDirectory) => hostingFsDelete(accountId, rel(path), isDirectory),
97	    uploadUrl: (dir) => q(dir),
98	    downloadUrl: (path) => q(path),
99	    // No chmod: the hosting backend has no chmod primitive, so the browser must
100	    // not offer a control that cannot work.
101	  };
102	}

1	/**
2	 * Per-game customization schema (MVP).
3	 *
4	 * A plain module (NO "use server") so it can be imported from server components,
5	 * "use server" action files AND the worker daemon alike — it holds no secrets and
6	 * performs no I/O.
7	 *
8	 * It declares, per game family, the available server *variants* (the loader/flavour
9	 * a player runs — Paper vs Vanilla, Carbon vs Oxide, …) and a versioned list of
10	 * *settings fields* that drive a dynamic UI. Fields are intentionally limited to
11	 * the handful of options players actually change, keyed on the game's own real
12	 * config keys (server.properties, PalWorldSettings.ini, cvars, …) — no invented
13	 * cvars — so a future real "apply" step can render them 1:1.
14	 *
15	 * Exports: `familyFor`, `schemaFor`, `validateConfig` plus the `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`
16	 * table and its types.
17	 */
18	
19	/** Bump when the field set changes in a way the worker/apply step must notice. */
20	export const GAME_CONFIG_VERSION = 1;
21	
22	export type FieldType = "enum" | "bool" | "int" | "string";
23	
24	/**
25	 * When a setting takes effect:
26	 *  - "deploy": needs a server restart / redeploy (world seed, tickrate, …)
27	 *  - "live":   can be pushed to a running server (motd, pvp, max players, …)
28	 * MVP treats both the same (simulated apply) but the UI surfaces the distinction.
29	 */
30	export type FieldPhase = "deploy" | "live";
31	
32	export type ConfigField = {
33	  /** The game's own config key (e.g. "max-players", "ServerPlayerMaxNum"). */
34	  key: string;
35	  label: string;
36	  /** UI grouping heading. */
37	  group: string;
38	  type: FieldType;
39	  default: string | number | boolean;
40	  /** enum only — {value,label} choices. */
41	  options?: { value: string; label: string }[];
42	  /**
43	   * enum only. When true and `options` is long, the settings UI renders a
44	   * type-to-filter combobox (components/customer/SearchableSelect.tsx)
45	   * instead of a plain native `<select>` — a flat dropdown of 100+ entries
46	   * has no usable way to find one. Leave unset for short option lists
47	   * (gamemode, difficulty, …), where a native select is simpler and fine.
48	   */
49	  searchable?: boolean;
50	  /** int only — inclusive bounds. */
51	  min?: number;
52	  max?: number;
53	  phase: FieldPhase;
54	  /** optional one-line helper shown under the field. */
55	  help?: string;
56	  /**
57	   * string fields only. When true, `validateConfig` rejects a blank value —
58	   * used for values with no sane platform default where the server is
59	   * genuinely non-functional / unjoinable without a customer-supplied
60	   * credential (e.g. DST's Klei cluster TOKEN — an online DST cluster
61	   * refuses to start at all without one). Enforced both at order-creation
62	   * time (lib/game-order.ts, BEFORE payment) and at settings-save time
63	   * (lib/actions-game-config.ts), so it gates checkout AND blocks a customer
64	   * from blanking it back out later. See DST.TOKEN below for the motivating
65	   * incident (added same-day as the family, 2026-08-31 audit).
66	   */
67	  required?: boolean;
68	  /**
69	   * Override the docker `-e KEY=` name that `applyGameConfigEnv`
70	   * (worker/game-variant.ts) substitutes into, when it differs from `key`.
71	   *
72	   * Found live 2026-09-11: Valheim's World Name field is keyed `"world"` (a
73	   * readable schema key, matches the game's own `-world` flag name) but the
74	   * lloesche/valheim-server image's actual env var is `WORLD_NAME`.
75	   * `applyGameConfigEnv` matches literally on `field.key`, so `-e world=`
76	   * never appeared in the setup script and the customer's chosen world name
77	   * was silently dropped at provisioning — every Valheim server booted on
78	   * the catalog's hardcoded default world regardless of what was ordered.
79	   * Set this whenever a field's readable schema key isn't the literal env
80	   * var name the image expects.
81	   */
82	  envKey?: string;
83	};

89	};

## Report: Wave 10 (Arma/CS16) reference pattern, SFTP/file-manager infra, and the mod-install async-job precedent

### 1. The Arma Reforger / CS 1.6 reference pattern (`/opt/nxeon-staging-newgames`, branch `feature/new-game-families-arma-cs16`)

Two commits on top of merge-base `cc3dabe0b81002f45125d6b28612c297c8c032bd` (= `main`):
- `59fba7a063` — "Add Arma Reforger + CS 1.6 game families (Wave 10)" (18 files, 771+/2-)
- `73c1e86d03` — "Wave 10: correct false test-provision claim, document honestly" (docs/seed-comment fix only)

Full file list touched (all absolute under `/opt/nxeon-staging-newgames/`):
```
app/(marketing)/arma-reforger-server-hosting/page.tsx
app/(marketing)/cs-16-server-hosting/page.tsx
app/sitemap.ts
components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx
components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts
docs/DOCUMENTATION.md
lib/game-config.ts
lib/game-control.ts
lib/game-mods.ts
lib/game-player-recommend.ts
lib/game-update-verify.ts
lib/games.ts
lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts
prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts
public/games/art/armareforger_hero.jpg / armareforger_poster.jpg
public/games/art/cs16_hero.jpg / cs16_poster.jpg
worker/index.ts
```
**No test files were added.** The existing generic fuzz test `/opt/nxeon-staging-newgames/test/games.test.ts` ("every string field on every family rejects control characters", line 56) picked up both new schemas automatically because it iterates `Object.keys(GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS)` rather than a hardcoded family list — no special-casing was needed. DOCUMENTATION.md's Wave 10 section (line 11215+) states the full test suite (1422 tests) was run with 0 regressions and TypeScript typecheck caught 4 exhaustiveness-check call sites that needed the new families added (that's why `lib/game-mods.ts`, `lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, `lib/game-update-verify.ts`, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` are all in the diff — the compiler forced them via `Record<GameFamily, …>`).

**`lib/game-config.ts` — `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` structure.** Type definitions at the top of the file (lines 22–97):
```ts
export type FieldType = "enum" | "bool" | "int" | "string";
export type FieldPhase = "deploy" | "live";
export type ConfigField = {
  key: string; label: string; group: string; type: FieldType;
  default: string | number | boolean;
  options?: { value: string; label: string }[]; searchable?: boolean;
  min?: number; max?: number; phase: FieldPhase; help?: string;
  required?: boolean;
  envKey?: string; // overrides the docker `-e KEY=` name when it differs from `key`
};
export type GameVariant = { id: string; label: string; description?: string };
export type FamilySchema = { family: string; label: string; variants: GameVariant[]; defaultVariant: string; fields: ConfigField[] };
```
`envKey`'s doc comment (lines 68–82) is itself the load-bearing precedent: it explains a real production bug found 2026-09-11 where Valheim's schema key `"world"` didn't match the image's actual env var `WORLD_NAME`, so the customer's chosen name was silently dropped at provisioning. `envKey` exists specifically to prevent that class of bug, and `worker/game-variant.ts`'s `applyGameConfigEnv` (line 137–159) is what consumes it: for each field it does `const envName = field.envKey ?? field.key;` then regex-substitutes `-e <envName>=...` in the setup script — if the placeholder for that env name doesn't literally exist in the script, the field is silently skipped (line 154 comment: "this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone").

The two new entries added at `lib/game-config.ts` lines ~1841–1930 (diff hunk after `SPACEENGINEERS`):
- `ARMAREFORGER` (`family: "armareforger"`) — 4 variants (conflict-everon/arland, gamemaster-everon, combatops-everon); 9 fields (`SERVER_NAME`, `SERVER_PASSWORD`, `MAX_PLAYERS`, `SCENARIO_ID` enum with 5 real `.conf` path options, `BATTLEYE` bool, `ADMINS`, `VISIBLE`, `RCON_PASSWORD`). **No `envKey` needed** — the comment explains `jsknnr/arma-reforger-server`'s env vars are already top-level and match the natural field names 1:1, unlike Valheim/V Rising/Unturned. `ADMIN_PASSWORD` is deliberately NOT a schema field (see worker/index.ts below).
- `CS16` (`family: "cs16"`) — 2 variants (amxx, vanilla); 7 fields, **every one carrying an explicit `envKey`** (`serverName`→`SERVER_NAME`, `map`→`MAP`, `maxPlayers`→`MAXPLAYERS`, `lanMode`→`SV_LAN`, `fastDownloadUrl`→`FAST_DL`, `adminSteamId`→`ADMIN_STEAM_ID`) because `archont94/counter-strike1.6`'s real env vars are UPPER_SNAKE_CASE and don't match camelCase keys — the comment explicitly calls this "the exact V-Rising-bug class this wave exists to avoid repeating." `rconPassword` has no `envKey` at all and is left un-set at provision time — it's genuinely not exposed as a docker env var on this image (verified live against the README), so the field's `help` text tells the customer to set it via SFTP/in-game instead of pretending to wire it up.

Both entries are registered in the `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` map at the bottom of the file (`armareforger: ARMAREFORGER, cs16: CS16,`).

**`worker/index.ts` diff (inside `buildCloudInit`, ~line 342–358).** Adds an `armareforger` branch to the existing password-generation ternary chain, alongside the pre-existing `palworld`/`rust`/`cs2` cases:
```ts
: server.osTemplate.family === "armareforger"
  ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { ADMIN_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
  : scriptWithJavaImage;
```
This is the mechanism by which a per-server secret gets minted at provision time instead of using the image's blank/absent default — `ADMIN_PASSWORD` is deliberately absent from `ARMAREFORGER`'s schema `fields` (see above) specifically so this code path is the only writer and a customer-typed value can't be silently discarded. CS16 needed no such treatment (no comparable secret field in its schema).

**Catalog wiring across `lib/*.ts`** (all diffs shown in full above): `lib/games.ts` adds `"armareforger", "cs16"` to `GAME_FAMILIES`, plus per-family entries in `GAME_DISPLAY` (name/glyph), `GAME_PORT` (`armareforger: {port:2001, protocol:"udp"}`, `cs16: {port:27015, protocol:"udp"}`), `GAME_ART_SLUG`, and `GAME_GENRES`. `lib/game-control.ts` adds both to `GAME_CONTROL` with `rcon: "none"` and `dataRoots: ["/opt/armareforger"]` / `["/opt/cs16"]` (confirmed against each family's own `-v host:container` bind mount in the seed's `setupScript`). `lib/game-mods.ts` adds `MOD_INFO` entries (Steam Workshop for Arma; Metamod+AMXX for CS16, both "no one-click installer, full file/SFTP access" — i.e. explicitly punting mod-install to the file manager). `lib/game-player-recommend.ts` adds rough RAM/CPU/disk-per-player curve fits. `lib/game-update-verify.ts` adds `SERVICE_HINT` entries. `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` adds `GAME_URL_SLUG` and `GAME_FLAVOR` entries (both **deliberately excluded** from `ACTIVE_GAME_FAMILIES`/the location-matrix pages — "ship the flagship page first").

**Marketing pages** at `app/(marketing)/arma-reforger-server-hosting/page.tsx` and `app/(marketing)/cs-16-server-hosting/page.tsx` (both read in full above) — standard flagship "Combined" game-landing template: `Metadata`, `FaqJsonLd`/`ProductOffersJsonLd`, `GameLandingCombined` fed from `PREVIEW_GAMES.armareforger`/`.cs16` (defined in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, ~137 new lines, plans/pricing copied verbatim from the seed's `GamePlan` rows), an FAQ block, and a "Related" links row.

**Sitemap**: `app/sitemap.ts` gets two new entries at the existing game-hosting section: `{ path: "/arma-reforger-server-hosting", priority: 0.7, freq: "monthly" }` and `{ path: "/cs-16-server-hosting", priority: 0.7, freq: "monthly" }`.

**`components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx`**: adds `GAME_VISUAL` entries (name/glyph/gradient colors) for both families, referencing the real Steam-CDN key art now in `public/games/art/`.

**DB seed — `prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts`** (full 219-line file read above, final state after both commits). Structure:
- `TEMPLATES: Template[]` — 2 entries (`armareforger`, `cs16`), each `{ family, name, setupScript, minRamMB, minDiskGB }`. `setupScript` is a single shell one-liner: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && mkdir -p /opt/<family> && [chown for arma] && docker run -d --name <family> --restart unless-stopped -p <ports> -e KEY='' ... -v /opt/<family>:<container-path> <image>:latest`.
- `TIERS: TierSpec[]` — 6 entries (3 per family) with `{ gameFamily, name, ramMB, cpuCores, diskGB, slots, priceCents, featured? }`. Arma: 6GB/16p $14.99, 10GB/32p $24.99 (featured), 16GB/64p $39.99. CS16: 1GB/16p $3.99, 2GB/24p $5.99 (featured), 3GB/32p $7.99.
- `main()` — upserts each `TEMPLATES` row into `db.osTemplate` (`where: { slug: t.family }`), collecting `templateIdByFamily`; then for each `TIERS` spec, picks the smallest active `db.plan` with `ramMB >= spec.ramMB` as `basePlanId`, and upserts (via a `findFirst` + create/update, no natural unique constraint) into `db.gamePlan` keyed by `{gameFamily, name}`.
- Run command documented at the top: `cd /opt/nxeon-staging && npx tsx prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts` (idempotent).
- **Critically, per the corrected commit `73c1e86d03`, this seed was never actually run against any database** — the header (lines 121–136) explains the session's auto-mode safety classifier correctly refused copying `/opt/nxeon/.env` (prod credentials) into the worktree, so no live Proxmox test-provision ever happened. Both `OsTemplate` rows exist only as this file's source, not as rows in any real DB. This is the single most important caveat for whoever picks this up: schema/marketing/catalog work is complete and typechecked, but neither family has been proven to actually boot on a VM.

The extensive header comments in both `lib/game-config.ts`'s new block and `prisma/seed-wave10-games.ts` also document the games that were investigated and deliberately **not** shipped (DayZ, ETS2/ATS, RuneScape/WoW, PUBG, StarRupture, Windrose, plus Hytale/SCUM/HumanitZ/VEIN left for later) — relevant if the next engineer is asked to pick up "the next wave" rather than just merge Arma/CS16.

---

### 2. SFTP / file-manager infrastructure for customers (`/opt/nxeon`, production)

**Model.** There is one `Server` Prisma model (`prisma/schema.prisma` line 707) shared by plain VPS and every game-server product — a game server is just a `Server` row with an `osTemplate` pointing at a game family and a `gamePlan`. Customers get **root SSH/SFTP to the whole VM**, not a scoped/jailed account and not a per-container shell. There is no separate "SFTP user" provisioning step for game families: the same root password minted during VM provisioning (`worker/index.ts` line ~706/757, `generatePassword()` → `encryptSecret()` → `Server.rootPasswordEnc`) is reused for both the control-panel SSH card and the file manager.

**Core transport — `/opt/nxeon/lib/sftp.ts`** (full file read above, 524 lines). Exports `serverRootPassword()` (decrypts `rootPasswordEnc`, falls back to legacy plaintext `rootPassword`), `connectionTarget()` (dedicated-IP servers → their own IP:22; NAT servers → their node's `publicIp` + the server's forwarded `sshPort`), and `withSftp()` which opens a real `ssh2-sftp-client` connection as `root` with the resolved password and always closes it in `finally`. Typed ops: `listDir`, `statPath`, `readFileText`/`writeFileText` (capped, e.g. 1 MB), `mkdirPath`, `renamePath`, `removePath`, `chmodPath`, `readFileBuffer`/`writeFileBuffer` (streaming, used by the upload/download route). Path safety: `normalizePath()` rejects relative paths, `..` traversal, NUL bytes, overlong paths; `sanitizeUploadName()` strips all directory components from a client filename so an upload can only ever land inside the fixed `UPLOAD_DIR = "/root/nxeon-uploads"`. `SANDBOX` mode (staging, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`) replaces every real SFTP call with an in-memory simulated filesystem per `server.id` — no real SSH connection opens on staging at all.

**Server actions — `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-files.ts`** (full file read above, 311 lines): `listFiles`, `readFile`, `saveFile`, `createFolder`, `renameEntry`, `deleteEntry`, `chmodEntry`, `uploadToServer` (base64 upload, hard-fixed to `UPLOAD_DIR`), `statEntry`. Every action re-derives the server via `ownedServer(serverId)` (`userId === caller` or `role === "ADMIN"`), rate-limits per user/op via `checkRateLimit`, and maps internal errors through `safeError()` so only path/size/ownership messages (never raw connection/protocol internals) reach the client.

**Route handler — `/opt/nxeon/app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts`** (full file read above): `GET ?path=&download=1` streams a file (`readFileBuffer`, forces `Content-Disposition: attachment`); `POST ?path=` accepts a multipart upload (up to 250 MB) and writes via `writeFileBuffer`, best-effort `mkdirPath`ing the target dir first. Both ownership-checked and rate-limited independently of the server actions above.

**Two backends, one component.** `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-types.ts` defines the `FileApi` interface (`list/read/save/mkdir/rename/remove/uploadUrl/downloadUrl?/chmod?`) that the file-manager UI is written against. `/opt/nxeon/lib/files-adapters.ts` provides `serverFileApi(serverId)` (wraps `lib/actions-files.ts`, absolute root-VM paths — this is what game servers use) and `hostingFileApi(accountId, root)` (wraps `lib/actions-hosting-fs.ts` for the separate chrooted shared-hosting product). This is genuinely a real SFTP client talking to the customer's own VM as root — **not** a shell-into-container mechanism; a game running inside a Docker container just happens to have its data bind-mounted at a host path like `/opt/cs16` or `/opt/armareforger` (per `GAME_CONTROL.dataRoots`), which the root SFTP session can browse like any other host directory.

**UI.** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx` (`ServerFileBrowser`, 467 lines) — a three-pane browser (lazy-loaded folder tree, listing, inline editor for small text-ish files under 1 MB) plus `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/files/UploadQueue.tsx` (219 lines, XHR-based multi-file upload queue hitting `uploadUrl`). Mounted in `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` at both the "Files" tab (line 600, `gameFilesPanel`) and the VPS "Files" tab (line 615, `filesPanel`) — same component, gated on `server.status === "RUNNING"`. Separately, `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/SftpAccess.tsx` (full file read above) renders a read-only credentials card (host/port/username `root`/password + ready-to-copy `sftp -P <port> root@<host>` and `ssh -p <port> root@<host>` command strings) so a customer can also point FileZilla/WinSCP/Cyberduck/OpenSSH directly at the box — this is shown on both the VPS Settings tab (line ~1422) and specifically called out as "the game branch" in a comment at line 877.

**Precedent for "drop in your own content" already exists platform-wide.** Marketing copy across many existing families explicitly tells customers to use file/FTP access to add their own content — e.g. `app/(marketing)/satisfactory-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload an existing save directly instead of starting fresh"), `app/(marketing)/ark-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("Full FTP file access lets you upload mods and edit GameUserSettings.ini/Game.ini"), `app/(marketing)/rust-server-hosting/page.tsx` ("upload custom maps, drop in plugins, hand-edit server.cfg"), `app/(marketing)/minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `mordhau-server-hosting/page.tsx`, `tf2-server-hosting/page.tsx`, and the generic per-family template generators `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` (lines ~552, 572, 809: "full file access means you can use it fully, or upload your own configs and mods") and `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` (lines ~529, 546, 991). This confirms the file manager is the platform's established, load-bearing answer to "how does a customer get their own content onto the server" — it is not a new concept to introduce.

---

### 3. Precedent: something lands on a server's filesystem as part of an async job

**`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mods.ts`** (full 376-line file read above) is the canonical example.

- **Queueing**: `installMod(serverId, modId)` / `uninstallMod(serverId, modId)` are `"use server"` actions. Each: authenticates + ownership-checks via `ownedServer()`, validates the mod against the server's family/variant, checks `hasInflightJob()` (`db.job.count({ where: { serverId, status: { in: ["QUEUED","RUNNING"] } } })` — enforces one in-flight job per server), upserts a `ServerMod` row to `status: "INSTALLING"` (or `"REMOVING"`), then `await db.job.create({ data: { type: "GAME_MOD_SYNC", serverId } })`. State lives in the DB row, not the job payload — "the same state-driven pattern as GAME_CONFIG (worker reads the DB, no per-op payloads to trust)" per the file's own header comment.
- **Prisma models** (`prisma/schema.prisma`): `Job` (line 1071: `id, type: JobType, status: JobStatus, payload: Json?, error, progress, step, attempts, serverId, createdAt, updatedAt`), `GameMod` (line 2944: the catalog — `gameFamily, name, slug, category, source, sourceId, url, modStringId, appliesToVariant, ...` plus a large block of upstream-verified metadata), `ServerMod` (line 3104: the per-server install-state join row — `serverId, modId, status ("INSTALLING"|"INSTALLED"|"FAILED"|"REMOVING"|"REMOVED"), version, error`, unique on `[serverId, modId]`).
- **Worker pickup**: `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts`'s main loop (lines 3183–3208) polls `db.job.findFirst({ where: { status: "QUEUED" }, orderBy: { createdAt: "asc" } })`, then atomically claims it with `db.job.updateMany({ where: { id, status: "QUEUED" }, data: { status: "RUNNING", attempts: increment } })` (count===1 wins the race), then dispatches via a flat `handlers: Record<string, (job: Job) => Promise<void>>` map (line 2215) — `GAME_MOD_SYNC: gameModSync` (line 2243).
- **Handler — `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-mods.ts`** (full 1000-line file read above): `gameModSync(job)` loads the server + all pending `ServerMod` rows, then branches three ways: `SANDBOX` (simulate only), `!REAL_ENABLED` (mark `FAILED` with an honest "not applied yet" message — never fakes success), or the real path. The real path is one of:
  - **Direct download installs** (`modrinth`, `spigotmc`, `umod`, `thunderstore`, `github`): resolve a direct download URL from the source's API (`resolveUrl()`), then open a plain SSH exec session (`withSsh`/`execRemote`, root@VM, same password source as the file manager via `connectionTarget`/`serverRootPassword` from `lib/sftp.ts`) and have the **VM itself `curl` the file** into a deterministic path computed by `modDirShell()` (e.g. Minecraft's `plugins`/`mods` dir found via `find`, or Valheim's fixed `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`). Uninstall is a plain `rm`.
  - **Steam Workshop installs** (`workshopSync` → per-family `applyXWorkshop` functions, ~600 lines): never downloads/mirrors the Workshop item itself. Either (a) writes the desired Workshop-ID list into a container env var and does a full stop/rename/recreate/verify/rollback container cycle (`recreateContainer`, lines 581–624 — systemd-unit-aware, rolls back to the `-old` container on failure) — used for ARK/DST/Squad/Soulmask; or (b) runs Valve's own `steamcmd` **once inside the customer's own container** (`docker exec <container> steamcmd +login anonymous ...`) to pull the item from Steam's CDN, then writes it into place over an SFTP channel (`withSftp`/`sftpWrite`, e.g. `applyL4d2Workshop` fetching `.vpk`s into `/opt/l4d2/addons/`, or `applyEmpyrionWorkshop` copying a fetched scenario into `Content/Scenarios/` and rewriting `dedicated.yaml`).
- **This is directly relevant precedent** for "place something onto a server's filesystem as part of an async job": the mechanism is always (1) a `Job` row with `type` + `serverId`, no trusted payload, (2) desired-state recorded on a DB row the worker reconciles toward, (3) file placement done either by SSH `exec` (`curl`/`docker exec steamcmd`) or by an SFTP channel opened with the exact same root-password auth as the customer-facing file manager — there's no separate "internal" transport.

**Free Minecraft tier (`freemc`) — a different, synchronous pattern, not a job queue.** Files found: `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts`, `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts`, `lib/actions-freemc-public.ts`, `lib/freemc-mod-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-command-catalog.ts`, `lib/freemc-capacity.ts`, `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` + `components/customer/freemc/v2/FreeMcHero.tsx`. **There is no `worker/freemc*.ts` file** — grepping `worker/*.ts` for "freemc"/"FreeMinecraft" returns nothing. Every freemc action (`switchFreeMinecraftGameType`, `applyFreeMinecraftGameMode`, `applyFreeMinecraftMods`, etc., all read in full above) does its work **synchronously inside the "use server" action itself**, via `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh`/`exec`/`shellQuote` helpers, against a single shared `freemc-host` VM (`db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" } })`) — never a `db.job.create`. The pattern per-user is: one Docker container per customer on the shared host, isolated by `-e LEVEL=<gameType>` and a per-user data path (`/opt/freemc/servers/<freeMinecraftServerId>`); switching game type / applying mods / mode is a full `docker rm -f` + `docker run -d` **container recreate** (`recreateGameTypeContainer` in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`) with an explicit roll-back-to-previous-config step on failure (mirrored in both `actions-freemc-worlds.ts` and `actions-freemc-mods.ts`). Content (extra plugins) is added purely by setting the `MODRINTH_PROJECTS` env var wider — `itzg/minecraft-server`'s own entrypoint does the actual download inside the container on boot; **Nxeon never writes a customer-supplied file into a freemc container** anywhere in these files. I did not find any freemc code path that stages/writes an arbitrary file before or during provisioning — mods/presets/inventory/roles are all env-var or RCON-driven, not file-drop.

---
